kultivator.cerita.quest.kota42_tujuh_mal: The seventh night. Hear his last verse.

Under the seventh moon, Li Zuixian slipped a jade into your hand. "The Drunken Eight Immortals Sword," he said. "My master gave it to me because I could never stand straight. You stand too straight. Learn to sway."
Drink peach-blossom wine with Li Zuixian for seven nights at his tavern.
Li Zuixian swears he will give his technique jade to whoever drinks with him for seven nights and does not fall asleep before the last verse.
kultivator.cerita.quest.kota42_utang_tig: The Wu family burned the IOU in the stall's stove. Whenever you come, your bowl holds noodles twice as long.
With a new wok and a new signboard, the Wu noodle stall is busy until late. The debt was cleared in a week, and four coins in ten of its profit are now yours.
Judge Bao struck out the unlawful interest and fined Master Shen double. Shen Wan no longer smiles at you, but half the market nods respectfully as you pass.
Pay the Wu family's debt to Master Shen at the Counting House.
Madam Wu asks for help. Hear her husband Wu Dalang's story at the noodle stall.
Invest in the Wu noodle stall and wait for the profit to clear the debt.
The stall's profit clears the debt.
The interest breaks the legal limit. Pay it yourself, take the case to Judge Bao, or invest in the noodle stall.
The Wu family's grandfather borrowed five taels from the Shen family. Three generations later, the interest has grown to two hundred.
Take the recalculated IOU to Judge Bao.
Judge Bao rules on the case.
Take grandfather Wu's IOU to Clerk Qiu at the Yamen to have it recalculated.
kultivator.cerita.quest.kota42_zhuazhou_: The baby grabbed a brush and a die at once. The two grandfathers laughed together for the first time in forty years, and accused each other of passing on the die.
Persuade Boss Li to see his grandchild.
Persuade Old Zhang to see his grandchild.
The Well Street couple have a baby in the Water City. At the zhuazhou ceremony the two grandfathers could make peace, if someone brings them there.
Attend the baby's zhuazhou in the Water City with both grandfathers.

Turn board: %1$s's name is written for that night, the ink still legible.
Turn board: its base is rotten and cracked, the wood wet and soft.
Word from %3$s: %2$s has been warned twice by the elder over water.
Word from %3$s: %1$s often extends his own turn.
“That ditch is not my affair. Water comes, water goes.”
“It was my turn tonight, but when I came the water was gone!”
“I only opened the gate briefly because my seedlings were wilting. %1$s exaggerates.”
%2$s restores the water turn and grants %1$s two extra nights.
%1$s is satisfied; %2$s is branded a cheat.
The claim is dismissed; the turn board is replaced with a marked stone.
The elder redraws the turns, both paddies get an equal share.
No victory, but the ditch keeps flowing.
“I heard the water wheel at an hour that was not %2$s's hour.”
“The turn board at the ditch was removed and shifted.”
“%2$s's soil really was cracked, the seedlings nearly dead. No wonder he panicked.”
“That turn board was rotten and fell by itself.”
%1$s accuses %2$s of opening the ditch gate out of turn so that his paddy ran dry.
kultivator.kota42.perkara.t.anak_tertaha: Shop ledger: the child is noted carrying goods daily, with no wage entry.
Shop ledger: a month of food and lodging is noted under the child's name.
Word from %3$s: the child's father once struck him in the market.
Word from %3$s: the child's father often gets drunk and vanishes for days.
“A child? I saw no one's child there.”
“My child has not come home for a month! He is used to lift sacks and wash dishes!”
“The child came by himself asking for food and work. I gave him a bed and a plate of rice.”
The child is returned, and %2$s pays a month's wage.
The claim is dismissed; the child stays for now and %1$s is warned.
%2$s is relieved; %1$s is angry and ashamed.
The child returns on conditions, and the hall appoints an elder to oversee.
Both sides are reluctant, but the child is calm.
“I saw the child carry two sacks of rice on his back, so small he is.”
“He is thin and his hands are red. %2$s does not let him out.”
“The child himself said he did not want to go home, saying his father is too strict.”
“%2$s fed him at the same table as his own children.”
%1$s accuses %2$s of keeping his child at the house and making the child work unpaid for a month.
kultivator.kota42.perkara.t.anjing_mengg: A torn scrap of a small trouser with deep tooth marks, the sign of a hard bite.
Dog tail hair torn and caught in a small hand, a sign of a forced pull.
Word from %3$s: %2$s's dog has barked fiercely at other children twice.
Word from %3$s: %2$s's dog is known to be gentle and often hugged by children.
“A dog? I saw no dog. I was sweeping.”
“That dog attacked my grandchild for no reason! Her leg bled!”
“My dog does not bite without cause. The grandchild pulled its tail.”
%2$s pays the healer and must tie his dog at busy hours.
%1$s is satisfied; %2$s lowers his head in shame.
The claim is dismissed; the dog is blameless and the child is taught to be kind to animals.
The healer's fee is split; the dog gets a bell and the child is taught to greet it.
The lane knows the rules now.
“I saw the dog lunge without barking first.”
“It was not tied though the lane was full of children.”
“The dog barked twice in warning, and only then bit.”
“The grandchild does like to tease animals in this lane.”
%1$s demands that %2$s pay the healer after his dog bit the grandchild's leg in the lane.
kultivator.kota42.perkara.t.atap_bocor.b: A tile shard in the yard: loose material, brittle edges.
A tile shard in the yard: clean and dense, a sign of fresh laying.
Builder's note: %2$s's roof was laid with cheap mixed tiles.
Builder's note: %2$s's roof was laid to the town standard.
kultivator.kota42.perkara.t.atap_bocor.d: “I did not see. There was a crash, and I shut my door.”
kultivator.kota42.perkara.t.atap_bocor.k: “His roof tiles fell again, this time nearly hitting my grandchild!”
“My roof was laid by a builder last month. The tiles were pushed by wind from %1$s's side.”
kultivator.kota42.perkara.t.atap_bocor.p: %2$s replaces the washing and relays his roof with good tiles.
%1$s is satisfied; %2$s complains of the cost.
The claim is dismissed; %1$s is told to prune his tree.
%2$s is relieved; %1$s grumbles about the tree.
They mend the roof and prune the tree together, lunch from %1$s.
kultivator.kota42.perkara.t.atap_bocor.s: “Two tiles broke on %1$s's washing line. I saw it myself.”
“The builder said the roof was sound, but yesterday's wind was strong.”
“The big tree in %1$s's yard snapped a bough onto that roof.”
kultivator.kota42.perkara.t.atap_bocor.t: %1$s demands that %2$s repair a roof whose tiles fell into his yard and spoiled the washing.
kultivator.kota42.perkara.t.cap_dipalsuk: The cloth examined: a two-feather crane seal, the ink not bleeding through the back.
The cloth examined: a two-feather crane seal identical to %1$s's old seal, ink bled through.
Hall seal register: %1$s's seal has three feathers, no two-feather seal is under his name.
Hall seal register: a two-feather seal is recorded for %1$s's workshop two years ago, then replaced.
“I only buy. I never check seals.”
“My seal shows a crane with three tail feathers. This cloth shows a crane with two. A copy!”
“That seal is genuine. I bought the cloth from %1$s's own workshop, perhaps he forgot.”
%2$s surrenders the counterfeit seal, pays a fine and withdraws all cloth from the market.
The claim is dismissed; the seal is genuine, %1$s is told to withdraw the charge.
Both seals are re-registered at the hall; the old cloth may sell out.
“I am a long-time customer of %1$s. This cloth is coarse, not as fine as his workshop's.”
“%2$s sells at half of %1$s's price. The same quality is impossible.”
“I saw the purchase note of that cloth at %1$s's workshop.”
“The two-feather crane seal was used by %1$s's workshop two years ago too.”
%1$s accuses %2$s of using a counterfeit trade seal on cloth sold in his workshop's name.
kultivator.kota42.perkara.t.giok_palsu.b: The bracelet scratched on a whetstone: it scratched, a sign of soft glass.
The bracelet scratched on a whetstone: unscratched, but cracked by an impact.
Caravan waybill: no mention of jade at all, only “ornamental stone”.
Caravan waybill: lists “green jade, six pieces” with the trader's stamp.
kultivator.kota42.perkara.t.giok_palsu.d: “Jade, glass... to me it all sparkles.”
kultivator.kota42.perkara.t.giok_palsu.k: “He swore it was Hetian jade! The goldsmith says it is glass.”
“I sold what I bought. I was cheated myself by a southern trader.”
kultivator.kota42.perkara.t.giok_palsu.p: %2$s refunds in full and posts a notice at his stall.
%1$s is satisfied; %2$s loses his name in the market.
The claim is dismissed; %1$s is asked to repay the inspection fee.
Half the price is refunded; the caravan is reported to the gate guard.
The true cheat may already be far away.
kultivator.kota42.perkara.t.giok_palsu.s: “I tapped the bracelet with my nail. It rang clear like a glass.”
“I saw %2$s sell three similar bracelets this week.”
“%2$s bought those bracelets from a caravan with a marked certificate.”
“%1$s dropped it once and blamed the seller when it cracked.”
kultivator.kota42.perkara.t.giok_palsu.t: %1$s demands that %2$s refund a jade bracelet found to be made of green glass.
kultivator.kota42.perkara.t.gosip_fitnah: Gossip chain: it begins with %3$s, who heard it from %2$s at the well.
Gossip chain: %3$s merely repeated %2$s without seeing anything.
A flour sample from %1$s's store: pure grain, no admixture.
A flour sample from %1$s's store: very fine and white, the milling hard to check.
“I only heard it from someone else, who was it... forgotten.”
“That gossip spread to the end of town and my customers left one by one!”
“I only told what I saw. %1$s's bread really is white, whiter than ordinary flour.”
%2$s retracts his gossip at the well and pays a fine.
%1$s has his name restored; %2$s is shamed.
The claim is dismissed because the gossip was only opinion, not slander.
%2$s is relieved; %1$s must prove his flour himself.
%1$s opens his store for inspection, and %2$s apologises.
“I have bought %1$s's flour every week for three years. There is no chalk in it.”
“The gossip started from %2$s's mouth, I heard it myself at the well.”
“The flour really is too white. I have been suspicious for a long time.”
“%1$s refuses to let anyone see his flour store.”
%1$s demands that %2$s retract the gossip that he mixes chalk into his flour.
kultivator.kota42.perkara.t.kebakaran_la: Charcoal piled in the kitchen, the stove still holding thick embers.
The stove charcoal is cold, but there are scorched embers in the thatch.
Watch record: before the fire, the guard saw %1$s's kitchen bright till late.
Watch record: a strong west wind since midnight, two other houses nearly burnt.
“I was asleep. I woke only when people shouted fire.”
“He left the stove burning and went to the market! The whole lane nearly burnt!”
“I put that stove out. The fire began on the roof, from an ember blown from another house.”
%2$s pays for the repair of kitchen and roof.
%1$s is satisfied; %2$s owes many people now.
The claim is dismissed; the fire is judged an accident of the wind.
%2$s is relieved; %1$s bears his own loss.
Costs are shared and all roofs are replaced with tile.
The lane is safer from fire in future.
“I saw %2$s leave the kitchen with the wok still hot.”
“The first smoke came from the kitchen window, not the roof.”
“That night a strong wind blew embers from the neighbouring kiln.”
“%1$s's thatch was as dry as twigs.”
%1$s demands that %2$s pay for the kitchen and roof burnt through a stove left alight.
kultivator.kota42.perkara.t.kerbau_masuk: The pen rope: frayed and torn at the end, pulled by force.
The pen rope: cut flat by a sharp blade.
Word from %3$s: %2$s often lets his buffalo graze on others' land.
Word from %3$s: %1$s once threatened to make %2$s sorry over the water.
“Buffalo? I was only passing with water. I saw nothing.”
“His buffalo trampled a quarter of my paddy! My harvest is gone!”
“My pen was locked. Someone opened its gate on purpose that night.”
%2$s pays for the ruined harvest and mends his pen.
The claim is dismissed; the buffalo was freed by someone else, and %1$s is told to find the culprit.
%2$s is relieved; %1$s loses harvest and suspicion.
They tend the remaining paddy together and share the yield.
The water grudge cools, at least until the dry season.
“I saw the buffalo walking alone on the dyke at dawn.”
“%2$s's pen fence has been rickety for ages, he never mended it.”
“The pen rope was cut clean, not snapped.”
“%1$s quarrelled with %2$s over water last week. I heard it.”
%1$s demands that %2$s pay for rice trampled by his buffalo, loose from its pen.
kultivator.kota42.perkara.t.kolam_ikan.b: Gold carp scales found in %2$s's basket.
A white heron feather left by the pond, with claw prints.
Word from %3$s: %2$s's bucket smelled of pond mud.
Word from %3$s: that heron has raided three other ponds this month.
kultivator.kota42.perkara.t.kolam_ikan.d: “Fish? I do not eat fish. I eat vegetables.”
kultivator.kota42.perkara.t.kolam_ikan.k: “The fish in my pond are halved in a week. No one but he takes them!”
“I fish in the river outside his fence. It is the heron that takes his fish.”
kultivator.kota42.perkara.t.kolam_ikan.p: %2$s pays for the fish and is barred from the pond.
The claim is dismissed; %1$s hangs a net over his pond.
The pond gets a net, and %2$s may fish on the river side.
kultivator.kota42.perkara.t.kolam_ikan.s: “At dawn I saw a shadow pole a small raft into that pond.”
“%2$s's bucket is always wet and full in the morning.”
“A white heron perches in the tree by that pond every morning.”
“%2$s has shared fish with neighbours for ages, from the river.”
kultivator.kota42.perkara.t.kolam_ikan.t: %1$s accuses %2$s of taking carp from his pond every dawn.
kultivator.kota42.perkara.t.kucing_terta: A long wheel mark in the corner dirt, a sign of braking too late.
A short, straight wheel mark; no sign of speed.
Word from %3$s: %2$s's cart often rushes in the morning market.
Word from %3$s: %1$s's cat is notorious and often slips into the road.
“A cat? I did not know about a cat. The market is full of cats.”
“His cart raced without looking! My cat was hit and is now lame!”
“That cat leapt right before the wheel. I pulled the reins with all my strength.”
%2$s pays the animal healer and hangs a bell on his cart.
The claim is dismissed; %1$s is told to keep his cat indoors.
The animal healer's fee is split; the cat is given a bell collar.
The cat heals and stays naughty.
“The cart rushed at the corner, I saw its left wheel mount the pavement.”
“%2$s was looking at the bun seller just then.”
“The cat was chasing a mouse and leapt from under a barrel.”
“The cart was slow with its full load. I was beside it.”
%1$s demands that %2$s compensate for his pet cat hit by a cart at the market corner.
Market register: the %1$s family name is listed at that corner until thirty years ago.
Market register: that corner was transferred to the %2$s family thirty years ago.
An old permit: the %1$s family mark, no sale recorded.
An old receipt with a red seal: the stall bought for fifteen taels.
“That stall? I always pass on the other side of the market.”
“My grandfather has traded at that corner since the town had a market. That is my family's stall!”
“My father bought that stall from %1$s thirty years ago. There is a receipt.”
The stall returns to %1$s; %2$s receives another corner with a year's rent cut.
The stall stays with %2$s per the receipt; %1$s is helped to a new corner.
The stall is shared: mornings for %1$s, afternoons for %2$s.
The market stays loud with two voices.
“I used to buy fish at that corner from %1$s's grandfather. I remember the smell of the sea.”
“The stall's base stone is carved with %1$s's family mark.”
“I was there at the purchase. The money was counted three times.”
“%1$s's grandfather did trade there once, then sold it.”
%1$s and %2$s contest the stall at the market corner near the well, which both claim as hereditary.
kultivator.kota42.perkara.t.mas_kawin.bu: The Matchmaker's red paper: the figure “ten” written in brush ink.
The Matchmaker's red paper: the figure “five”, and below it a trace of old scratching.
Word from %3$s: %2$s's family bought new land after the betrothal.
Word from %3$s: %2$s's family had two failed harvests in a row.
kultivator.kota42.perkara.t.mas_kawin.du: “It was noisy, I did not hear the figure. Do not ask me.”
kultivator.kota42.perkara.t.mas_kawin.kl: “Ten taels of silver and two bolts of silk, promised before the Matchmaker! Now he says he does not remember.”
“What I promised was one bolt of silk and five taels. %1$s adds to it every time he tells it.”
kultivator.kota42.perkara.t.mas_kawin.pu: %2$s pays the ten-tael bride price as the Matchmaker wrote.
The bride price stays five taels; the betrothal goes on.
%2$s is relieved; %1$s grumbles but still attends the feast.
Seven and a half taels, and the two families eat together.
Both sides hold back for their children's sake.
kultivator.kota42.perkara.t.mas_kawin.sa: “I was there when they clasped hands. The word ‘ten’ was clear.”
“The Matchmaker wrote the figure on red paper. She is never wrong.”
“I stood behind them, and what I heard was ‘five’, not ‘ten’.”
“Two days later %1$s complained that the bride price was too cheap.”
kultivator.kota42.perkara.t.mas_kawin.te: %1$s demands that %2$s keep the bride price promised for their children's betrothal.
kultivator.kota42.perkara.t.obat_palsu.b: Residue in the draught bottle: clear sugar grains, no leaf flecks.
Residue in the draught bottle: fine root flecks at the bottom, a sign of a real brew.
Word from %3$s: two other buyers complained of the same to %2$s.
Word from %3$s: %2$s's draughts once healed half the street.
kultivator.kota42.perkara.t.obat_palsu.d: “Medicine is the healer's business, not mine.”
kultivator.kota42.perkara.t.obat_palsu.k: “My child drank that draught three days and the fever did not drop. It only tasted sweet!”
“My draught is real, made of roots and leaves. The child's fever was simply worse than I guessed.”
kultivator.kota42.perkara.t.obat_palsu.p: %2$s refunds, hands the rest of the draught to the town healer, and is barred from selling for a month.
The claim is dismissed; %1$s is advised not to stop a treatment halfway.
%2$s is relieved; %1$s is ashamed and worried.
Half the money is refunded, and the town healer examines the child free.
The child recovers, both sides shake hands.
kultivator.kota42.perkara.t.obat_palsu.s: “I tasted what was left of the draught. It was only sugar and a little ginger.”
“I saw %2$s stirring a basin with rock sugar, no root at all.”
“I drank the same draught and my fever went down overnight.”
“%1$s gave the child too little and stopped on the second day.”
kultivator.kota42.perkara.t.obat_palsu.t: %1$s demands a refund from %2$s for a fever draught that proved to be only sugar water.
kultivator.kota42.perkara.t.perkelahian_: A chair splinter with finger marks and wine dregs on the wood.
A table splinter stuck high in the wall: not where one defends oneself.
Word from %3$s: %2$s was banned from three other wine shops.
Word from %3$s: %1$s's shop is known for watered-down wine.
“I was asleep in the corner. I saw nothing.”
“He threw the first chair! I saw it with my own eyes!”
“I only defended myself. %1$s and his guests started the insults.”
The brawl at the wine shop
%2$s pays for all damage and works three days at the shop.
%1$s is satisfied; %2$s is shunned at other shops.
%1$s bears the damage himself and is warned about watered wine.
%2$s is relieved; %1$s loses face before his customers.
Costs are split and both shake hands before the guard.
The shop is busy again, the brawl forgotten.
“I heard a chair snap, then %2$s shouted while lifting a table.”
“He was drunk before midnight and refused to leave.”
“The waiter spilled wine on %2$s's clothes and laughed. That was the spark.”
“%1$s was the first to push, then blamed the other.”
%1$s demands that %2$s pay for two tables and a wine jar broken in last night's brawl.
kultivator.kota42.perkara.t.pernikahan_b: The feast shopping list: all ingredients paid in full under %1$s's name.
Debt record: the bride-to-be is listed owing thirty taels at the hall.
Word from %3$s: %2$s has cancelled two earlier betrothals.
Word from %3$s: %1$s knew of the debt from the start and covered it up.
“A wedding? I was not invited, so I do not know.”
“The tent is booked, the food bought, the invitations sent! And he cancels with no reason!”
“I have a reason: the bride-to-be hid a large debt. %1$s knew himself and kept silent.”
%2$s repays half the feast cost and apologises publicly.
The claim is dismissed; the cancellation is valid because the debt was hidden.
The feast food is given to the temple and costs are split.
The cancelled feast is not wasted.
“I cooked two days for that feast. All the ingredients were bought before my eyes.”
“%2$s only said ‘I changed my mind’, no other reason.”
“I heard the lender dunning at the door of that bride-to-be.”
“%1$s once said ‘marry first, debts can wait’.”
%1$s demands that %2$s repay the cost of a wedding feast cancelled unilaterally a week before the day.
kultivator.kota42.perkara.t.pohon_tumban: A trunk cross-section: brown, hollow and soft inside, a sign of long rot.
A trunk cross-section: hard and damp inside, snapped by wind pressure.
The carpenter's note: two months ago he warned %2$s about that tree.
The carpenter's note: that tree was inspected in spring and declared healthy.
“A tree? There are many on this road. I know not which.”
“I told him three times that tree was rotten! Now my fence is smashed!”
“That tree was healthy. The strong wind felled it, not rot.”
%2$s pays for the fence and fells two other trees that look rotten.
The claim is dismissed; the wind is declared the sole cause.
%2$s is relieved; %1$s must pay for his own fence.
The fence is replaced together, the remaining trees checked by the town carpenter.
“I heard %1$s warn %2$s about that tree last month.”
“The trunk was hollow inside, I saw after it fell.”
“The wind that night felled two other trees on this road.”
“%2$s pruned its boughs last season. He tended that tree.”
%1$s demands that %2$s pay for a fence crushed by a locust tree long complained of as rotten.
kultivator.kota42.perkara.t.sewa_kuda.bu: Saddle: the left hoof shoe full of small stones and fresh abrasions.
Saddle: a cloth wrap on the left foot, stained with old soil.
Word from %3$s: %2$s is known for riding hired horses till they foam.
Word from %3$s: %1$s twice sold a sick horse as a sound one.
kultivator.kota42.perkara.t.sewa_kuda.du: “Horses? Plenty on that road. I recall none.”
kultivator.kota42.perkara.t.sewa_kuda.kl: “My horse left sound and came back lame! He surely rode it without mercy.”
“That horse was already lame before I hired it. %1$s hid it with a cloth on its leg.”
kultivator.kota42.perkara.t.sewa_kuda.pu: %2$s pays half the horse's price and the animal healer.
The claim is dismissed; %1$s pays for the horse's care for concealing it.
Both pay the animal healer together and the horse is lent free to the elder.
The horse heals, the grudge subsides.
kultivator.kota42.perkara.t.sewa_kuda.sa: “I saw that horse sound and spirited when it left.”
“%2$s rode it over the stony road, in the rain.”
“That horse has often lifted its left foot since last season.”
“I saw the cloth on its leg. %1$s knew something was wrong.”
kultivator.kota42.perkara.t.sewa_kuda.te: %1$s demands that %2$s pay for a horse lamed after two days hired to the next town.
kultivator.kota42.perkara.t.sumur_tercem: Indigo deposit on the well wall, only on the side facing the shop.
A drowned rat near the well bottom, its fur already shedding.
Word from %3$s: the dye shop was warned by the elder for dumping carelessly.
Word from %3$s: %1$s has long wanted that shop moved from his lane.
“Well water? I drink from the river.”
“The well water is blue and smells. The children have stomach aches. This must be from his dye shop!”
“My shop drains waste to the ditch, not the well. The water smells because a dead rat is in it.”
%2$s moves his dye rinsing to the riverbank and pays for the well's cleaning.
The claim is dismissed; the well is cleaned of the rat and covered with a board.
The well is covered, and the shop ditch rerouted away from it.
“I smelled the same indigo at the well and in %2$s's ditch.”
“His dye buckets are always rinsed by the well, I often see it.”
“I cleaned that well myself this morning, found a dead rat near the bottom.”
“The shop ditch flows to the river, not the well.”

kultivator.kota42.wayang.hakim_bao.sumbe: Source: the Judge Bao tales (Bao Gong An)

kultivator.kota42.wayang.hua_mulan.judul: Hua Mulan Takes Her Father's Place
kultivator.kota42.wayang.hua_mulan.lore: Puppeteer Su whispers: in the ballad, when her comrades learned who she was they stood amazed, for male and female hares are equally hard to tell apart when they run.
kultivator.kota42.wayang.hua_mulan.pembu: The lamp is lit. The sound of a loom comes from behind the screen: clack-click-clack, clack-click-clack, then stops.
kultivator.kota42.wayang.hua_mulan.penut: The gong greets Mulan's return. Behind the screen, the loom sounds again, this time soft and happy.
kultivator.kota42.wayang.hua_mulan.sumbe: Source: the Ballad of Mulan (Mulan Shi)
kultivator.kota42.wayang.kera_sakti.baba: We walk for the scriptures, not for speed.

Master, where shall we be tomorrow?
Wherever, as long as we keep walking.
The day's journey ends. Master and disciple bow to each other beneath the moon. The white horse grazes. The screen dims.
kultivator.kota42.wayang.kera_sakti.lore: A thank-you from Puppeteer Su: the Monkey King has seventy-two transformations, and as many ways to watch him.
kultivator.kota42.wayang.kera_sakti.pemb: Puppeteer Su raises the lamp wick. On the glowing screen, the hide cured for a hundred days lives again.
kultivator.kota42.wayang.kera_sakti.penu: The last gong rings, and the silhouettes become hide again. The audience applauds for a long while.
kultivator.kota42.wayang.kera_sakti.sumb: Source: Wu Cheng'en, Journey to the West (Xiyou Ji)
kultivator.kota42.wayang.ular_putih.baba: Thank you, sir. Lend me your umbrella as far as the lakeshore.
Rain on Broken Bridge. A young physician lends his umbrella to a woman in white, and neither knows that spring has just chosen them.
Sister, there are crowds here. Do not look at the sky.
I know. I only want to look at the market.
Two sisters walk the town road, and anyone who passes feels the air grow cooler.
Stand aside, monk! My sister never hurt anyone!
The love of man and serpent will not end well.
The monk Fahai arrives with his ringed staff. He says, "That woman is a serpent." Xiaoqing draws her sword, and the screen trembles.
Fahai chases Bai Suzhen back to that bridge. The water of West Lake rises behind the screen, and the entire audience holds its breath.
kultivator.kota42.wayang.ular_putih.judu: The White Snake at West Lake
kultivator.kota42.wayang.ular_putih.lore: Puppeteer Su says: in the white snake tale, the umbrella is always older than its owner, and the rain always more faithful than a promise.
kultivator.kota42.wayang.ular_putih.pemb: The oil lamp flickers, and rain falls across the screen. A red umbrella opens by West Lake.
kultivator.kota42.wayang.ular_putih.penu: The screen turns white as lake mist, then goes dark. Someone in the back row wipes their eyes.
kultivator.kota42.wayang.ular_putih.sumb: Source: the White Snake legend (Baishe Zhuan)
